input.new_string:
## Metrics

quill-server serves Prometheus metrics at `/metrics`:

| Metric | Type | Labels | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `quill_renders_total` | counter | `theme`, `result` | renders finished; `result` is `ok` or `error` |
| `quill_render_seconds` | histogram | `theme` | time to render one document |
| `quill_render_queue_depth` | gauge | | renders waiting for a worker |

The Go runtime and process metrics (`go_*`, `process_*`) are there too. The Grafana dashboard is `deploy/grafana/quill-render.json`.

## Logs

message.content: Something's off. The p95 and p99 lines are perfectly flat at exactly 10 seconds, all day. The sample books take 30 to 60 seconds, I timed some by hand. p50 looks plausible.

input.command: kubectl -n quill-staging exec deploy/quill-server -- wget -qO- localhost:8080/metrics | grep 'quill_render_seconds_bucket{theme="paper"' | tail -6

content.text:
That explains the flat line. I never set Buckets on the histogram, so client_golang used prometheus.DefBuckets, which go from 5 ms up to 10 seconds and stop there. 186 of the 498 paper renders took longer than 10 seconds and all of them landed in the +Inf bucket, where the histogram knows nothing about their duration. When a quantile falls in the +Inf bucket, histogram_quantile returns the upper bound of the highest finite bucket, which is 10. So p95 and p99 can never show more than 10 s, however long renders take; p50 is fine because the median is well under 10 s.

The default buckets suit web requests, not renders that run for a minute. The histogram needs explicit buckets that reach past the longest render, for example exponential buckets from 0.25 s doubling up to 128 s.

message.content: Do that, up to a couple of minutes is right.

content.content:
--- PASS: TestRenderBucketsReachTwoMinutes (0.00s)
ok  	quillmark/internal/metrics	0.007s
--- PASS: TestQueueCountsRenders (0.21s)
ok  	quillmark/internal/render	0.498s

input.command: make deploy-staging 2>&1 | tail -1 && sleep 1800 && curl -s 'http://prometheus.monitoring:9090/api/v1/query' --data-urlencode 'query=histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(quill_render_seconds_bucket{namespace="quill-staging"}[30m])))' | jq -r '.data.result[0].value[1]'

content.text:
After half an hour of renders on staging, p99 is 52.3 seconds, in line with your timings, and it moves with the data instead of sitting on 10.

In short: the render histogram used client_golang's default buckets, which top out at 10 s; every longer render fell into +Inf, and histogram_quantile reports the highest finite bound, 10 s, for any quantile that lands there. quill_render_seconds now has explicit buckets, ExponentialBuckets(0.25, 2, 10), from 0.25 s to 128 s, with a test that the top bucket reaches two minutes.
